answer: Each collapsed cluster gets one canyon weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 86 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 175 times the capital for one share. The mesa report reveals the merge explicitly at each knoll. A farm of 2734 identities would post 1090 proofs and burn roughly 6 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
